sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by anti-HA western blot and flow cytometry (L7). Membrane expression confirmed by immunofluorescence in HEK293 cells for rat ortholog N-terminal Myc/HA constructs (L3). Receptor used in RUSH trafficking assays monitoring surface delivery (L5). Signaling function not explicitly assayed in these clips.
sites.rationale: AGTR2 has no signal peptide (residue 1 is Met, the mature N-terminus), so the extracellular N-terminal domain (residues 1–45, 45 aa from TM1) is the only extracellular terminus available for a prepended tag. The 'NHA' nomenclature in L7 unambiguously encodes an N-terminal HA tag on full-length human AT2R, and surface detection by anti-HA antibody confirms the tag is accessible on the cell surface. Because no specific residue number is named in any clip, the position is topology-derived: insert_after_residue = 0 is the sole valid junction for an N-terminal prepend on a signal-peptide-free GPCR. The rat AT2R N-terminal Myc/HA data (L1/L3/L4) and the 3HA human AT2R trafficking data (L5) independently corroborate this site. L7 (PMC6770525): adenoviral AdNHA-AT2R construct expresses full-length human AT2R with an N-terminal HA tag ('NHA' = N-terminal HA) in MDA-MB-231 cells; surface presence confirmed by anti-HA western blot and flow cytometry. L1/L3/L4 (PMC3466278) independently report N-terminal Myc- and HA-tagged rat AT2R (close ortholog, ~92% identity) with confirmed membrane expression in HEK293 cells. L5 (PMC10551652) reports a 3HA-tagged human AT2R used in RUSH trafficking assays.

sources.claim: So, we overexpressed AT2R in these cells using an adenovirus encoding AT2R (AdNHA-AT2R), which contained a bicistronic vector that permits co-expression of both the angiotensin receptor coupled to an HA-tag and the green fluorescent protein (GFP) [ 24 ].

literature_notes: Four ledger lines (L1, L2, L3, L4) describe C-terminal GFP and FLAG tags on rat AT2R; these are placed after residue 363, which falls in the intracellular C-tail (IC 319–363) and therefore do not qualify as extracellular surface-tag sites — they are recorded in other_positions. No ledger line reports a tag insertion in any of the four extracellular loops (ECL1 103–119, ECL2 180–208, ECL3 279–297) at a named residue, so no internal loop site is proposed. L5 and L6 describe 3HA-tagged human AT2R constructs used in RUSH assays but do not specify the tag position by residue; given L7's explicit 'NHA' nomenclature and the standard GPCR N-terminal tagging convention, these are treated as additional support for the N-terminal site rather than independent sites. No ledger line supports any insertion in ECL1, ECL2, or ECL3 of AGTR2 or a close ortholog.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal FLAG and GFP tags on rat AT2R (L1/L2/L3/L4) are appended after the last residue (S363), which lies in the intracellular C-tail (IC 319–363); these are valid intracellular labels but not extracellular surface-tag sites.
